title: Open extension preserves finite constructibility and its cohomological interval
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $n\geq1$; put $P_n=A/t^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), let $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion, and assume that $\ell$ is invertible on $V$ [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient ring sheaves $(P_n)_U,(P_n)_V$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $j_!$ denote exact extension by zero on module sheaves and its termwise functor on their unbounded derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For integers $a\leq b$ and $C\in D^b_c(U,P_n)$ in the finite-torsion sense [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], suppose $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-cohomological-support]. Then $j_!C\in D^b_c(V,P_n)$ and $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. More precisely, for every $r$ one has $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)\cong j_!\mathcal H^r(C)$; any finite constructible locally closed stratification for $\mathcal H^r(C)$ on $U$, together with a reduced closed complement $Z=V\setminus U$, is a constructible locally closed stratification on $V$ on which this sheaf is locally constant with finite stalks, with zero restriction on $Z$. Empty strata may be omitted.

proof.text: Apply the existing exactness instances of sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero. The exact-functor mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso gives H^r(j_!C) ≅ j_!H^r(C), with the direction reversed from its standard H^r(-) followed by j_! orientation. This is the cohomology comparison already descended through localization; no new representative argument is needed.

proof.text: Use the existing extension_constructible theorem in Sheaf.Paper.OpenExtensionFiniteTor, made public without changing its type or proof. It realizes the following etale-origin argument. For constructibility of each output cohomology sheaf, use proEtaleModuleRestriction_constructible_iff and intrinsicRealization_restriction to move to fixed-scalar sheaves. The fixed-module constructible-origin theorem gives a constructible etale model. The open immersion is quasi-compact on the locally Noetherian ambient scheme. Extend the etale model by zero using IsConstructibleSheaf.openImmersionLowerShriek_of_quasiCompact, and apply the etale/pro-etale extension comparison. The same coefficient realization then gives constructibility of j_!H^r(C), and the cohomology isomorphism transports it to H^r(j_!C).

source.place: Tags 099Y and 09AK; etale-cohomology extension by zero; existing source-library constructibility argument

proof.text: For the restriction identities use the canonical openSquarePullbackModel (the unit-normalized coordinate comparison recorded with the open-square construction), sfIntrinsicPullbackComp, and the fully faithful open-extension adjunction unit. They give (s ≫ j)^*(j_!H) ≅ s^*H for every stratum map s. For a map g whose range misses the open, j^*g_*N has zero sections: its fibre-product objects are empty. The two adjunctions then make Hom(g^*j_!H,N) a singleton. Thus g^*j_!H is zero, exactly as in the existing isZero_upperStar_openImmersionLowerShriek. Transport this through the same coefficient equivalences to tensor pullback.

source.place: Tag 09BN; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03D8; open unit and disjoint restriction adjunction argument

proof.text: For the supplied complement i:Z→V and supplied stratification S, define D on Option(Fin S.n) by D(none)=i and D(some k)=S.immersion k ≫ j, as objects of Over V. Their ranges cover V by the original coverage and the complementary-range identity. They are pairwise disjoint, using injectivity of j on two original strata and complementary ranges in the other cases. Retain exactly the subtype Q of indices not in omitted. Every point in a range forces its index to lie in Q, since an omitted domain is empty. Choose the ordinary finite-type equivalence Fin(card Q) ≃ Q. The resulting domains and immersions are the original D objects, so their required Over identifications are reflexivity isomorphisms. Immersion composition makes each range locally closed; NoetherianSpace makes it constructible.

source.place: Tag 005L; properties.tex Tag 01OZ; explicit finite partition and deletion of empty domains

proof.text: Compose the pullback of the cohomology comparison with the stratum restriction isomorphism. Transport each supplied local model across this isomorphism by overFunctor.mapIso. Applying the actual geometric-module-stalk functor gives an underlying linear equivalence, so the given finite stalks remain finite. On the complement use the zero restriction: the singleton identity cover and constant zero module witness local constancy, and the additive stalk functor sends zero to a zero module with a singleton underlying set. Apply these two properties as a predicate on the D objects in the preceding construction. Reuse the existing locallyConstant_of_isZero, finite_stalk_of_isZero and finite_stalk_of_iso theorems in Sheaf.Paper.ProEtaleBoundedConstructibleTriangulated, made public without type or proof changes; the universe-flexible local models are transported directly.

Exact extension carries zero cohomology to zero cohomology. Hence output cohomological support is a subset of input support. The supplied finite input support remains finite, and its inclusion in [a,b] gives the same output interval. Combine this with constructibility of every output cohomology sheaf and with the explicit stratification conclusions. The subtype construction also allows zero strata when all domains are empty; the constructibility predicate itself retains its existing positive-stratification convention through the etale comparison.
